sermon.title: One Other Ministry
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message, Pastor David G. Kincer continues on the baptism of the Holy Ghost, teaching that it brings understanding of God’s word. He covers Proverbs 1:23 and Acts 2:38, why the apostles needed their understanding opened, the hardened heart, 1 Corinthians 14 on tongues, and why love and maturity are the greatest signs.

Editor notes: he reads “Ephesians 5:8” for “be filled with the Spirit, be not drunk with wine” (about 0:00); that wording is Ephesians 5:18, shown here. At about 47:00 he reads “1 Corinthians 14:16” for “what shall I profit you unless I speak to you”; those words are 1 Corinthians 14:6, shown here. Several names of ministers (about 10:20 and 35:50) and a street name (about 25:00) were garbled in the captions and are marked [unclear]. chunks.section_question: Where does he say the Holy Spirit is promised? (Ephesians 5:18, Proverbs 1:23, Joel 2:28, Acts 2:38)
chunks.short_answer: He says he is “a firm promoter of the baptism of the Holy Ghost” and wants “everything that God offers to get me into the divine nature.” He says Proverbs 1:23, “turn at my reproof,” holds the same promise as Joel 2:28, “I will pour out my spirit unto you,” and as Acts 2:38, so “the same promise in the Old Testament is the same promise in the New.”
chunks.text:
Ephesians 5:8 says, “Be filled with the Spirit, be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess.” And that word “excess” does not mean where you get drunk to intoxicate you, you know, you’re stumbling around. It means the word means it leads to undisciplined behavior. Don’t get drunk with wine, because it brings you to undisciplined, uncontrollable behavior. That’s what alcohol does, and so does marijuana and other drugs. So we are going to continue on the baptism of the Holy Spirit and show you another one of its ministers, of ministries rather, to those who receive the baptism of the Holy Ghost. I am a firm promoter of the baptism of the Holy Ghost because the Bible promotes the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and I also experienced the baptism of the Holy Ghost, so I know what I’m talking about from both the Bible and my experience. Okay.

Now, I’m going to be sharing with you some things that I didn’t know until the last few years, when God stepped back and waited for me to seek him to find out some new truth. Okay, now a further look at the Holy Spirit and its effect on us: partaking, participating in the divine nature. If I need something to empower me and help me partake of the divine nature, I don’t want to dismiss it, do you? I want everything that God offers to get me into the divine nature. Could that be an amen?

And the Holy Spirit is one of these promises that he promised to give us, to bring us into the divine nature. Proverbs 1:23. Pentecostal has never used this scripture; they always use Joel 2:28. Charismatics, same way: Joel 2:28, Acts 2, Joel 2:28 and Acts 2, Joel 2:28, Acts 2, that’s it. But the Holy Ghost is mentioned all throughout the Old Testament, and the same words: “I will pour out.” “Turn at my reproof.” Okay, “turn” means repent. Repent at my reproof, when I come to you with the prophets, when I come to you with preachers preaching the word. If you will repent and turn from your sins, admit you’re wrong, does that sound like a New Testament principle? Absolutely.

It wasn’t, that’s not a New Testament principle, it’s since the beginning principle. You know, so many Christians think the New Testament just obliterated, just ended the Old Testament. Folks, all this stuff is in the Old Testament, all of it. So here in Proverbs 1:23: “Turn at my reproof,” and he says if you will repent, I’ll do something for you: “Behold, I will pour out my spirit unto you.” Wow. Same word “pour” as Joel used: “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.” Here it is in Proverbs, okay: “I will pour out my spirit unto you.”

Now, we got to understand that this is the same statement in the New Testament, Acts 2:38: “Repent and be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission, forgiveness, of sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.” Okay, the same promise in the Old Testament is the same promise in the New. So when Dave Kincer heard the preaching of the gospel, and he confessed his sins and asked Jesus to forgive his sins, and I renounced those sins, knew they were wrong, and I purposed to turn from them. Now, I didn’t turn from all of them in one day; I just purposed to turn from them. It took me some time to get rid of some sins. How many took you a little time to get rid of? Yeah, yeah. But my goal, my heart, was to renounce these things and get rid of them. Then I became a candidate for the baptism of the Holy Ghost.

chunks.section_question: What does Philip in Samaria show about the baptism of the Holy Ghost? (Acts 8)
chunks.short_answer: He says Philip preached in Samaria with healings, belief and water baptism, and that “days later Peter came down and laid hands on them and they got the Holy Ghost.” He says “the Holy Ghost was a different experience than water baptism, than salvation, than miracles and signs and wonders and hearing the preaching of the word. We need them all.” He calls the claim that you get it in water baptism “a bunch of baloney.”
chunks.text:
Now, you find in Acts 8 a story of Philip going down and preaching the gospel to the Samaritans, okay, the city of Samaria. He preached the gospel, there were healings and miracles going on, the people believed. Great joy filled the city. The people repented, the people were baptized in water, tremendous thing. Now, folks, I have been trying for 40 years to get the church to see this. Philip went down and preached the gospel. Jesus said that he will work with the word, with signs following, if we would preach his gospel, preach his gospel, not man’s ideas, he would back it up with miracles and signs and wonders. And we don’t see that today, and one of the reasons we don’t see it in America.

We’re seeing it overseas, whether people want to accept it or not, it’s happening overseas in South America, Central America, Africa, Asia. It’s happening. Okay, the Book of Acts is happening. The miracles happened, they were baptized in water, then days later Peter came down and laid hands on them and they got the Holy Ghost. The Holy Ghost was a different experience than water baptism, than salvation, than miracles and signs and wonders and hearing the preaching of the word. We need them all. Could that be an amen? And I’ve been trying for 40 years to get God’s people to get their spiritual minds opened up to this: that when God arises, his enemies are scattered; if he be lifted up, he’ll draw all men to him. And the key to this is the power of the word and the power of the Holy Ghost, and get the mechanics out, get the ritual out, get our opinions out, and stick to the word, and God will come and do his thing, and people will come. People will come when there’s real miracles going on.

People will come when there’s a real move of God changing people’s lives. See a homosexual changing his life, that’s a miracle. An alcoholic changing his life, that’s a miracle, and the word’s going to get out. You know, advertisement, you can’t get better advertisement than that. But we have gotten distracted in America, and we’ve been distracted for decades. And today I want to make sure that you know what I’m trying to get across to you. Amen. What the Holy Ghost is trying to get across to you. All right, so these people that say, “I got baptized in the Holy Ghost when I got baptized in water,” that’s a bunch of baloney. These people that say there’s no indication or sign that you are filled with the Holy Ghost, that’s a bunch of baloney. They are different experiences, and we need them all. And this Holy Ghost is a promise given to us to be partakers of the divine nature, and the Bible says without him we can do what? Nothing.

chunks.section_question: Does the baptism do it all? (Proverbs 1:23, 2 Timothy 2:15, John 14:26)
chunks.short_answer: He says “there’s no magical baptism, water or Holy Ghost,” and “you got to put some effort into this.” He says “the Holy Ghost will drive you into the word,” citing John 14:26, and that the Holy Ghost “will only reveal to you what Jesus Christ himself taught and the disciples passed on,” not any minister’s opinions.
chunks.text:
Folks, we need Jesus, we need the Holy Ghost. Amen. Now then, he says what he will do when he poured out his spirit unto you: “I will make known my words unto you.” Boy, that would be nice if God’s people really understood the Bible, and you can raise your hand and actually say, “I understand from Genesis to Revelation the whole Bible.” You’re a wise people. And you know, one of the reasons is you haven’t really read it consistently or studied it. The Bible says, “Study to show yourself approved.” Put some time into this book. We just want, you know, water baptism does it all, or the Holy Ghost baptism does it all. No, you got to put some effort into this. I mean, will you raise your hand and say, “Yeah, I agree with that, I got to put some effort into this”? There’s no magical baptism, water or Holy Ghost.

The Holy Ghost will drive you into the word. Okay, how many would like for the Holy Ghost to come and give you understanding of his word? It’s important that you respond, because God is looking, and you can respond mechanically, or you can be distracted like some of these teens over here giggling and so forth, writing notes between each other and distracting the other guy, or you can get serious and you can attain these things. Huh? So publicly responding, I found as a young Christian, was a very important part of my growth in God. John 14:26: “The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, shall teach you all things.” See, the New Testament confirms and verifies what God said he would do in Proverbs. The Holy Ghost will teach you all things and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.

We got to get away from [unclear] and [unclear] and [unclear] and whatever, and we got to get back to Jesus Christ and the apostles’ doctrine. And I’m not trying to knock that, I’m just telling you people are worshiping ministers, and they’re looking to ministers to tell them what to do, when they need to go to that Bible and get their understanding open to what Jesus Christ himself said. And that’s all the Holy Ghost will reveal to you. He won’t reveal to you [unclear]’s opinions, he won’t reveal to you [unclear]’s opinions or Billy Graham’s opinions. The Holy Ghost will only reveal to you what Jesus Christ himself taught and the disciples passed on. Amen. And I told you before, I read many books when I was a young Christian, 30, 35 books a year, but nothing surpassed the Bible. I finally realized I don’t need human books, I need the Holy Spirit revealing this Bible to me.

chunks.section_question: Why does he say books should never replace the Bible? (1 Corinthians 2:13)
chunks.short_answer: He says “books should never replace the Bible” and that you “come to the level of the real author, the Holy Spirit and Jesus Christ.” Citing 1 Corinthians 2:13, he says the apostles spoke “not in words which man’s intellect teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches,” and says he has “heard a lot of human intellect” and repents of passing it on.
chunks.text:
Amen. A lot of those books were wrong, they were just flat-out wrong. You cannot write a book on your experience in God; you must write a book on Jesus’s experience in God, because he is the fullness, and the apostles are the fullness, they had it. Are you there? Because all you’re going to do is come to the level of the author. When you go to the Bible, you’ll come to the level of the real author, the Holy Spirit and Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. I’m not against books, but books should never replace the Bible.

New Testament verification, 1 Corinthians 2:13: “These things we speak, not in words which man’s intellect teaches, but which the Holy Spirit teaches.” And that seems to be lacking in America today. We have intellect, and I watched a bunch of shows on TV this week, and I just heard a lot of human intellect, that’s all I heard. And I, I repent. Did I go, “God, am I like that? Am I just going to the Bible with human intellect and passing on human intellect?” Forgive me if I am; that is horrible. He said we don’t teach with our intellect but with the Holy Spirit, what the Holy Spirit teaches. See, the apostles only taught what the Holy Spirit gave them to say.

chunks.section_question: Why did the apostles need their understanding opened? (Luke 24:45, Isaiah 28:10)
chunks.short_answer: He says the apostles had walked with Jesus “three and a half years,” seen miracles and preached, “and yet they didn’t understand until he came and opened their understanding.” He says “you got to realize you don’t know everything just because you accepted Christ,” and compares growth to school: “God isn’t like American public schools that just pass you because you attend church.”
chunks.text:
Wouldn’t that be good if our ministers would do that? Wouldn’t it be good if the congregation would do that? Good Lord, we have so many opinions and we all think we’re right. So I want you to know the New Testament backs up this Old Testament promise, and so we go back to the divine nature of Christ. Luke 24:45: “Then Jesus opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.” Now listen, those apostles had been walking with him for three and a half years. They had heard the Sermon on the Mount over and over and over and over and over. You see, they had heard his teachings of the kingdom over and over and over and over and over. They had heard him say he was going to die on the cross and rise again, over and over and over and over, for three and a half years.

They had seen the miracles, they were participators in miracles and casting out demons and healing the sick and preaching the gospel and people saved, they were ministers of the gospel, and yet they didn’t understand until he came and opened their understanding. And this is step number one: you got to realize you don’t know everything just because you accepted Christ. And you don’t know everything because your church has some articles of faith. You don’t even know their articles of faith. I guarantee you right now this congregation cannot tell me 10% of the truths in our articles of faith, and our articles of faith covers the Bible. Are you there? So we need Christ to, what, come along and open our understanding, and he does it. The Bible says little by little, line upon line, precept on precept.

You got to get kindergarten passed before you go to first grade, second grade, third grade, high school, college in God. So if you don’t respond to the kindergarten message, you’re not going to move on. God isn’t like American public schools that just pass you because you attend church. He only passes you to the next level when you are participators in the first one, in the previous one you got. That, I mean, you can hear high messages and it doesn’t matter; only Jesus can reveal it to you, I don’t care who’s preaching. Okay, now if Bible characters needed more understanding, so may we need more understanding. Joseph and Mary: now remember, Joseph and Mary had angels coming and visited them. Mary had an angel coming and visit her and told her she was going to have Jesus, the Messiah, the Savior of the world.

chunks.section_question: What does he say about Mary, Joseph and “delegated ministers”? (Luke 2:49)
chunks.short_answer: He says Mary and Joseph both had angelic visits, yet when Jesus was 12 he “had more understanding than the priests in the temple.” He says Joseph was not a stepfather but “a delegated minister,” and that “the Pope is a delegated minister, mainly by the Catholic Church, not God,” while a pastor “better be from God himself.” These are his own views.
chunks.text:
I mean, man, she got the message straight, and she had the Holy Ghost overshadowing her, and that which was birthed in her was conceived by God himself. chunks.section_question: Is God hiding it from people, and why was he afraid of God? (Luke 9:44)

chunks.text:
Christians, when I talk with them, their understanding is so shallow I am shocked that they want to live in that kind of, you know, state when God has promised so much. Do you get my point here? These people had experienced some tremendous things in God, yet when Jesus said, “I must be about my Father’s business,” they didn’t understand what he said. And if they needed more understanding, is it possible we do? Absolutely, and we got to get it the way the Bible says to get it. All right, the Jews and the 12 apostles, Luke 9:44. Jesus just healed a demon-possessed boy, all right, and then Jesus tells the apostles and the Jews there, “The Son of Man shall be delivered into the hands of men,” but they understood not, and it was hid from them. Now, remember I told you, you can’t get second grade until you passed first grade.

You see, God is the one that will keep it hidden until you have done what’s necessary to get the new understanding. Now, don’t go blaming your ignorance on God. And right quick, boy, I just see people going, “Well, it’s, I’m like I am because of God.” I’m like I am because, no, you’re not. God has offered us all these things. This is what they come out with: they see Jesus transfigured and he’s talking to Moses and Elijah, and so this is the revelation they got: we need to build a temple for Jesus, a temple for Moses, and a temple for Elijah. And this is where we’re at in America, Europe: we got the Baptists, we got the Lutheran for Luther, we got the Presbyterians for the [unclear], we got this temple for this person, this temple, Calvin temples, we got all these temples, we got [unclear] Street temple. Do you have eyes but you see not, and do you have ears but you hear not?” You see not, it’s not the Devil, it’s not your preacher, it’s not your parents, it’s not your neighborhood, it’s not your nation, it is you. chunks.short_answer: He says Israel’s ignorance was “some of it themselves, not God,” citing Acts 7:25, Psalm 106:7 and Deuteronomy 5:29, “Oh, that there was a heart in them that they would fear me.” He says the second coming is a hidden thing: “no one understands that, and they won’t understand it till the time comes,” and that others have been “changing their doctrines on the second coming.”
chunks.text:
Hallelujah. Israel in Egypt coming out, Acts 7:25: “Moses supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them, but they understood not.” Psalm 106:7 says, “Our fathers understood not your wonders,” your miracles, your judgments in Egypt, and most Christians don’t understand that either. They just talk about the miracles, they have no idea why that is. There. Huh? And a lot of us suppose we know something and we don’t know beans, and we need the Holy Ghost to, what, open our understanding.

Now, if these Bible characters needed it, and here’s, uh, the tabernacle in the wilderness. Israel’s ignorance was some of it themselves, not God. God had some things hidden, but he had most of his stuff revealed, and we read in Deuteronomy 5:29, “Oh, that there was such a heart.” Now, what do we find just a few verses back? It’s our hard heart that was the problem, right? The hard heart. What do we find in the Old Testament? What was Israel’s problem? The heart, the hard heart. They were a hardheaded people. “Oh, that there was a heart in them that they would fear me, keep my commandments always, and that things would go well with them and their children forever.” You see, yes, there were some things, the Messiah was a hidden thing. And so certain things will be hid, but there’s not anything that’s going to affect us in not being participators of the divine nature. Okay, it’s not tongues as languages, it is languages that were acquired by a supernatural means, and this is what the quarrel is about in the church world in America and Europe. Okay, “my understanding is” what?

Unfruitful. Okay. Tongues does not give me understanding. Us Pentecostals have got to understand that. You just hear what these preachers say over and over and over and over; we need to go and see what Paul said. Are you with me? Okay: “My spirit prays but my understanding is unfruitful.” Okay, like Bible characters, we may experience the presence and the power of God, and we did in the Pentecostal charismatic services.

I’m telling you, the presence of God would come, you could feel his presence, and that’s what we want here, that’s a purpose of worship, to bring the presence of Jesus so he can open understanding and change people’s lives. You may experience gifts of the Spirit but not increase our understanding. Why do [unclear] and [unclear] and them fall when they were supposed to be filled with the Holy Ghost? Because they weren’t letting the Holy Ghost give them what? Understanding. So they could meet God in prayer and worship and praise, and miracles happen and gifts of the Spirit’s going on, and I’ve told you this over and over and over. I go to third world countries and God’s healing people and doing things, and the ministers are having sex with the women and robbing the church of the money and doing these things, and when I approach them and I tell them this is not right, they simply say, “Look at the results.” Well, the results are because God loves people and he’s meeting people. chunks.section_question: What does he say about waves of revival and how tongues should be used? (1 Corinthians 14:16, 14:9)
chunks.short_answer: He says “every wave that preceded hindered the new wave God was bringing in,” and that a “tsunami” is coming. He says “there’s no record of him having an interpreter on his ministry team,” and that “don’t forbid to speak with tongues.” Reading 1 Corinthians 14:6 (which he calls 14:16), he says speaking should be “by revelation, by knowledge, by prophecy, and by teaching,” and that “tongues are for a purpose.”
chunks.text:
You know, the Lutherans, you know, they come out, and then the Baptists came out and the Lutherans persecuted them, the Methodists come out and the Baptists and the Lutherans persecuted them, and I can go on down the line to the Alliance church with divine healing and the Pentecostal church with, you know, the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Every wave that preceded hindered the new wave God was bringing in. That’s the way us Christians are. We can’t realize there’s a big wave back there, a tsunami, that’s going to just sweep over the world and over the church and change everything. Now, he had just quoted this scripture, in the law it is written, “With men of other tongues and other lips will I speak to this people, yet for all that they will not hear me.”

He had just quoted this scripture when he says tongues are a sign for those who are not believers. And remember, on the day of Pentecost they spoke in languages of the earth, and they didn’t need an interpreter because the people of the language was there, knowing what they were saying. And that’s when God began to deal with me and say, you know, if Paul spoke in tongues more than them all, and he said when the believers come together he would rather prophesy and speak in tongue, where did he speak in tongues? Now, it took a few years to get this into my cranial vacuum. I’m not like you guys, you just, yeah, got it. So when Paul went out to all these nations, he went out everywhere, all dialects, all languages, he had that gift of tongues to speak in their language the things of God.

There’s no record of him having an interpreter on his ministry team. Giving you something to think about. I’m going to expound on it. Watch this: “Don’t forbid to speak with tongues,” and people are forbidding it, saying it’s of the Devil and everything else. 1 Corinthians 14:16: “If I come to you speaking with tongues,” what’s tongues? The word tongue, language supernaturally acquired, not naturally acquired: “what shall I profit you unless I speak to you?” Now listen to this, and us Pentecostals, I have never heard this preached, and I didn’t see it till just recently.

If I come to you speaking in languages acquired supernaturally, “what shall I profit you unless I speak either in languages acquired supernaturally, by revelation, by knowledge, by prophecy, and by teaching?” Oh my Lord, it just opened up the error we’ve been in for a hundred years. Now, do I have to speak in a heavenly language or a supernatural language to speak by revelation, by knowledge, by prophecy, and teaching? No. But if I speak in a tongue it should be one of these four, or I profit [unclear] anything. And all of a sudden, tongues are not for you to draw attention to yourself and feel good.

Tongues are for a purpose. It’s assigned to the unbeliever, and when these languages are spoken, it brings revelation. And I spoke by revelation in many third world countries without tongues. I would just be speaking and God would reveal to me, open up a scripture to me, and I’m learning while they’re learning. Okay, I could speak also by prophecy, the divine inspiration of the Holy Ghost, while I was preaching. I had all of these sources working on my behalf when I preached, and I wasn’t speaking in tongues. But if we’re going to speak in tongues, it should have what? The same purpose. Are you there? Now, how many know that would be a sign to an unbeliever? 1 Corinthians 14:9: “Unless you utter by tongues words easy to understand, how shall it be known what is spoken?”

chunks.section_question: What does he tell Pentecostals and non-Pentecostals? (1 Corinthians 13:1–3, 14:40)
chunks.short_answer: He says “we need the Holy Ghost to preach, to teach, to give a word of wisdom, to give a word of knowledge, to heal,” and asks non-Pentecostals, “where is the fruit of the baptism of the Holy Ghost in your life?” He says “you don’t stop flying airplanes because one crashed” and that “God honors the principle of response.” He closes with 1 Corinthians 13 and “let all things be done decently and in order.”
chunks.text:
And the problem with Pentecostals and non-Pentecostals is we don’t really perceive that we need the Holy Ghost to preach, to teach, to give a word of wisdom, to give a word of knowledge, to heal. We need the Holy Ghost to initiate it. And so the non-Pentecostals, they just said, “Not for today, I got the Holy Spirit when I was baptized in water.” The Catholics say they got the Holy Spirit when they had the commencement, you know, and they went through catechism, and, you know, that they got the Holy Ghost there. Listen, if you had the Holy Ghost, why are you living the way you’re living?

And so I challenge the non-Pentecostals: where is the fruit of the baptism of the Holy Ghost in your life? They say there’s no sign, there’s no indication of being filled with the Holy Ghost. Yes, there is. You’re going to have a compelling for the word of God so you can get understanding. Your understanding is going to keep increasing, your behavior is going to change, the way you approach God is going to change. You may not have raised your hand before, you may not have clapped before, but as I tell the fundamentalist, the Bible says, “Clap your hands, all ye people,” that includes fundamentalists, “and shout to God with a voice of triumph.” Are you there?

“I would that men, all men everywhere, raise up holy hands without wrath or doubt,” and that includes fundamentalists. Who gave you the right to disobey God’s word because you were raised a certain way? You got to break away and follow God’s word, and God honors the principle of response. Wow, that was good. Amen. That’s what I tell the Catholics. Oh, I love them and I share with them, but I am direct with them. Understanding we need from the Holy Spirit.

Okay, this is what we got to get in our cranial vacuum: “Though I have the gift of prophecy, understand all mysteries, have all knowledge, have all faith,” the faith camp, the prophecy camps, they’re all in here, “though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor,” the focus on the poor, it’s all in here, “and though I give my body to be burned,” a martyr for Jesus, a martyr for my church, martyr for my opinions, “and have not love, I am nothing, and it profits me nothing.” See, we can experience, and this is what the Catholics and the other Protestant churches don’t understand, is that God can move in Pentecostals and charismatics and gifts and all these things, and they not have understanding, and they behave in a manner and do things that any idiot of the Bible knows is not Bible. And there’s no Bible for “slain in the Spirit,” falling backwards, and there’s no Bible for that, and anybody with any common sense is going to go, “You guys are nuts.” And that’s what Paul said. He said they’re going to think you’re crazy.

But I tell my Protestant friends that are non-Pentecostals and Catholics, you don’t throw out a truth because someone shipwrecks it. It’s still a truth. You don’t stop flying airplanes because one crashed. You don’t stop driving a car because one crashed. It’s the drivers that crash, it’s the people. The baptism of the Holy Ghost is for us, it’s a key to turning America around back to God, and anybody can have it. This church can have it. Amen. And the Bible says, say at the end of this, “Let all things be done decently and in order.” You see, and when we get out of order, we look stupid, but we need to do it right. Amen.

chunks.section_question: How does he end? Love and growing up (1 Corinthians 14:20, 13:11)
chunks.short_answer: He says “love is the result of the Spirit” and “pride and division is the result of human intellect,” and that “the greatest sign is the greatest commandment.” He urges bringing a woman who had an abortion to “forgiveness and change and reconciliation in her life.” Citing “be not children in understanding,” he asks, “Can we grow out of Christian childhood and into a responsible, mature Christian?”
chunks.text:
We need to do it right. Love is the result of the Spirit, the Holy Spirit’s impartation of understanding. Pride and division is the result of human intellect. That’s my statement. The baptism of the Holy Ghost, the greatest sign is the greatest commandment: to love God. The great commission, the great commandment is to love God, love your neighbor, love yourself, love your wife, love your husband, love your children. That’s the greatest sign of the Holy Ghost baptism that I know of, is when he brings you to that dimension of love. And this is what the Holy Ghost will do for you, and he’ll give you a heart to love the Catholics, knowing they’re wrong, to love the homosexual.

How are you going to reach them if you don’t love them? To love the lady who had an abortion and bring her to the place where she can find forgiveness and change and reconciliation in her life. How are you going to do it? For God so loved the world, he didn’t tongue the world, he didn’t [unclear] the world, he loved the world, and came and taught us in the condition we are in. And that is my high recommendation to this church: we need this baptism of the Holy Ghost, we need its expressions in our services, so unbelievers and believers can grow in God. “When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, and I thought as a child.

When I became a mature man, I put away childish things.” Did you get that? Is your understanding Christian childishness? Is that the level you’re at? God wants you to know you can grow up. Doesn’t that sound exciting? I mean, who wants to stay a baby all their life? “Be not children in understanding, but in understanding be” what? Mature. Isn’t that a powerful challenge from God to us? Can we grow out of Christian childhood and into a responsible, mature Christian that not only believes the things of God and sees the things of God but possesses the things of God?

Absolutely you can, and you will be a powerful, effective force in the earth when you do this. All claim to have the Holy Ghost, yet we argue over baby doctrines, support lifestyles that the Holy Ghost opposes and support doctrines that the Holy Ghost opposes, and everybody claims to be filled with the Holy Ghost.
